notes.title: Patch 4 released!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/b4bd7eaf7dcec9697524ec7fe0db67063e1db24b.png[/img]

Hello everyone,

A new patch is available today for TDF 23!

[h2]Short Version[/h2]

[list]
[*] Update of database (rider ratings and world champion jerseys).
[*] Update of jerseys (Vuelta kit and national teams).
[*] Correction of inconsistencies in the wearing of distinctive jerseys in My Tour.
[*] Correction of non-respected fitness peaks in Pro Team and Pro Leader.
[*] New kit without special jerseys in My Tour.
[/list]

[h2]Long Version[/h2]

[list]
[*] Database: update of ratings.
[*] Database: correction of the nationality of the DSM team, from German to Dutch.
[*] Database: update of world champions (M. Van der Poel and R. Evenepoel).
[*] Visual adjustment: update (race, podium, UI) of national team jerseys (Germany, Denmark, Great Britain, Norway).
[*] Visual adjustment: update of jerseys of the Vuelta kit (4 leader jerseys, Arkéa Samsic and Astana).
[*] Visual adjustment: the world champion no longer wears his champion's helmet in the world championship.
[*] Visual adjustment: the time-trial champions' jerseys are no longer worn in the team time-trial.
[*] Visual adjustment: champions' jerseys are now worn in My Tour if national teams are used.
[*] Gameplay: correction of non-respected fitness peaks when starting line-ups are changed during the season in Pro Team and Pro Leader.
[*] Gameplay: correction to legendary riders available for the world championships in Pro Team.
[*] Interface: correction of inverted Mountain and Time-trial medals on Pro Leader's progression page.
[*] Interface: opponents not fully recovered from a fall are indicated on the results' page.
[*] Possibility to use a jersey kit without Tour de France, Giro or Vuelta special jerseys in My Tour.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch 3 released
notes.content:
Hello riders, 

The third update for Tour de France 2023 has arrived!

Here's the changelog:
[list]
[*] AI adjustment: riders now give it their all to compete for best climber points.
[*] AI adjustment: team-mates who are stronger than the polka-dot jersey wearer no longer wait for him when the latter is dropped.
[*] AI adjustment: improvement to the creation of the grupetto so that riders who could target a good GC position no longer ease up and needlessly lose time.

[*] Gameplay adjustment: bad race-day condition has more impact during time-trials, meaning larger gaps between riders in good condition and those who are struggling.
[*] Visual adjustment: update of existing national champions.
[*] Visual adjustment: addition of new national champions' jerseys (Slovenia, United States, Denmark, Ireland).
[*] Correction of a bug: incorrect commentary on the Vulcania > Issoire stage.
[*] Correction of a bug: in Pro Leader mode, Bonus Points now earn progression points.
[*] Update of database: official Tour de France starting line-ups are present.
[*] Update of database: rider ratings.
[*] Update of database: addition of a missing Lotto Dstny rider (Jarne Van de Paar).
[*] Update of database: removal of Gino Mäder (Bahrain Victorious).
[*] Update of database: correction to a rider costing 0€ (S.Tu).
[*] Removal of the mountains classification bonus on stage 1 of the TDF.
[/list]

notes.title: New patch released
notes.content:
The second update for Tour de France is here, with a series of fixes and improvements.

[b]A few details before reading the changelog:[/b]
- The "Open Beta" and "Default" branches are the same, however you must switch to the default branch to play the race of the moment, otherwise your result will not be taken into consideration.
- The challenges of the moment will end earlier on Thursday morning to allow for the update.
- Please also note that this patch does not contain the official start list for the 2023 TDF or the jerseys, as the patch was submitted before this information became official.

[u]Here's the list of fixes in tomorrow's update:[/u]

[list][*] Fix for the incorrect nationality of Welays Hagos Berhe (team Jayco Alula)[/list][list][*] Fix for the message ‘Failed to send the results’ in Race of the Moment[/list][list][*] Fix for a case where it was impossible to sprint in the last kilometers[/list][list][*] Fix for a crash using teams not registered by default in Vlaanderen Classic[/list][list][*] Improvement of the passage of the Champs-Elysées tunnel to favor massive sprints[/list][list][*] Adjustment of the frequency of falls so that they can happen a little later in the Tour de France[/list][list][*] Addition of Tour de France jerseys for teams Uno-X and Bahrain[/list][list][*] Fix for a wrong jersey displayed in Pro mode simulation if the team has a specific jersey for the Tour de France[/list][list][*] Modification of AI opponents on the final sprint phase with a new method to estimate sprint distances so that the sprinter and his train trigger their effort at the best time[/list][list][*] Modified generic helmets for more realism[/list][list][*] Fix for the Editor interface to correctly display arrows when changing notes[/list][list][*] Application of the Tour regulations on all My Tour races, regardless of the startlist[/list][i][list][*] PC Only: update of the “Controller required” warning screen[/list][list][*] PC Only: keyboard support to enter names[/list][/i]

Regarding Gino Mäder, we have decided in agreement with his team to withdraw him from the game. He is currently still available for the Paris Nice but will soon be withdrawn from all races.
Once again, the entire Cyanide and Nacon teams would like to offer their deepest condolences to his family, friends and team.

notes.title: Devblog 3 - Game mode improvements
notes.content:
Hello and welcome to another TDF23 devblog!

For this devblog, we won't be focusing on just one area but rather on a range of changes made to enhance and streamline the experience when using the various game modes.

So, let's start right away with the Pro Team and Pro Leader modes. This year, our goal was to give you more flexibility in these modes. To achieve this, we added new settings that you can adjust when you create a new game. You can choose your starting budget independently of the difficulty selected so you can progress faster or slower according to your preference. 

In Pro Leader mode, two new options have been added. The first allows you to adjust the level of teammates assigned at the start of the game. So, you can start with a strong team from the very first season or with a weaker team for a harder challenge. 

The second option sets an age limit so you can create a team composed of U25 riders only. As well as these new starting settings, you now have the option to change the difficulty of races before the start of each event. So, there's no longer any need to restart a season if you feel you chose the wrong difficulty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/f120fe11996eb15ec43c077ac82593e5a7c7585d.png[/img]

Following the addition of the Medium Mountain rating, a new series of objectives has been added to the existing ones to improve Pro Leader mode. However, even though the Downhill rating has been replaced by the Agility rating (see devblog 1), this doesn't mean there are new career objectives. We decided to set Agility to maximum for all new riders. We thought it was more fun to be able to catch up during downhill stretches at the beginning of your career rather than fall behind at the top of the first hills. 

We have also made some visual changes for these modes with refreshed jerseys when creating your team and a new distinctive jersey added for the leader of the Pro Cycling ranking. Finally, for these modes, the way the variant stages* work has also been changed so that they are only offered if you have already competed in the race. Therefore, the Tour de France route won't change from the second season; only when you have completed it for the first time.

[previewyoutube=EK26-DQA0CE;full][/previewyoutube]

Now let's take a look at the Race and My Tour modes. Like the Pro Team and Pro Leader modes, we wanted to streamline certain areas. First, we removed the experience (XP) system. Although it worked well a few years ago when the game was focused on the Tour de France and a few "bonus" races, with the new events and modes now in the game, unlocking the same races every year no longer made any sense. All the game's content is available at launch. Whether it's races, stages, Legend difficulty or the team of legends (which gains three new champions this year), it is all available right from the start.

In terms of content, the World Championships can now take place on four different types of routes (flat, hill, medium mountain, mountain) instead of three. Three new teams have also been added to the World Championships: Denmark, the United States and Switzerland. The "Open Tour" race, which is only found in the Race mode, has new rules: only U25 riders (25 years old and under) can take part in this event.

[previewyoutube=9aaqRGc3T3c;full][/previewyoutube]

We have used a little artistic licence by adding mountain rankings to the Monuments. Don't worry! It doesn't ruin these events because it "only" displays the profile of hill climbs such as the Roche-au-Faucon, the Poggio and the Mur de Sormano. However, if you create a My Tour that includes a classic, such as Liège-Bastogne-Liège, the climbs will grant points for the best climber classification, which provides greater consistency in a stage race. Note that in stage races, a summary of the various winners and jersey wearers will be displayed at the end of the event, so you can track how the race unfolded. Each event will have its own kit of distinctive jerseys to make a clearer separation between them.

[previewyoutube=TIWRSDUqxPE;full][/previewyoutube]

To further improve the seamlessness of the game experience, several interfaces have been redesigned. Some of them now have a navigation shortcut to move to the next page quicker (when creating a customized Tour and the calendar page of the Pro Team / Pro Leader modes), while others are now clearer and therefore more user friendly (Transfers, Online Ladders, Team Composition, Fast-Forward pages).

A final devblog is planned before the game releases. It will focus on new features and changes to races.

[i]* Variant stages are stages that replace the official stages so that an event's route isn't exactly the same from season to season.[/i]

[b][i]Tour de France 2023[/i] sera disponible le 8 Juin 2023.[/b]

notes.title: Devblog 2 - Challenges of the Moment mode
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

For our second devblog on TDF23, we're going to take a look at Challenges of the Moment. Having appeared last year as Race of the Moment, the aim of this mode is to regularly offer you new events to refresh objectives and challenges. In line with this, the mode is being expanded with Downhill Challenges.

 Some of you were disappointed that they disappeared for a few years, but they are back this year! While the goal is still to ride down a hill as quickly as possible, these challenges are now only available for a limited time. In the same way that the objective of Race Challenges is to achieve the best position possible in a given leaderboard with a predefined team, in Downhill Challenges you need to get down hills as quickly as possible to place well in online leaderboards. For this type of challenge, it's not strategy and tactics you need but rather dexterity and speed!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/806b7dcdf723c9a8f6f4c498022088128adb862e.png[/img]

You will need to be adaptable because every downhill must be raced with a particular rider, and as explained in the previous devblog (insert link), the Agility rating will greatly influence the way you ride downhill. You can't approach bends in the same way with an A+ rider and a D rider. A ghost of your best downhill will help you improve throughout your attempts. At the end of each challenge, your best time will unlock new badges and earn points towards your progression in the online leaderboards.

[previewyoutube=sBttCPYDge0;full]https://youtu.be/sBttCPYDge0[/previewyoutube]

As for Race of the Moment, it is also changing with the introduction of a new type of ranking proposed by the community during the 2022 beta: ranking based on time difference. During these events, the objective is to win the event with as big a lead as possible over the next person in the overall classification. 

The bigger the time difference, the better your result in the race. In situations where the predefined team means winning the race is impossible, the goal is to finish as close as possible to the winner. In this case, the smaller the time difference between you and the winner, the better your result for the online leaderboard.

New strategic options have also been added with the introduction of condition boosts. These consumables give a boost to race-day condition for the whole team. You can use a maximum of two of them before each stage (and thus reach exceptional condition for your whole team), but use them wisely because there are only a limited number of them available. 

It's up to you to decide whether to spread them out over the entire race or save them up for particular stages. In the online leaderboards, you can see the stages where other players have used their condition boosts.

So, these are the changes for Challenge of the Moment mode. In the next TDF devblog, we'll look at the different historic game modes and various other topics. Till next time!

notes.title: New ratings for riders
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

In this first devblog for [b]Tour de France 2023[/b], we'll take a look at rider ratings and two new mechanics introduced this year: [i]Agility[/i] and [i]Medium Mountain[/i].

[h2]AGILITY NOTE[/h2]

[i]Agility [/i]is a new rating that replaces the Downhill rating. Based on a 5-tier scale (A+, A, B, C and D), it differentiates between riders while playing the game, influencing their ability to turn and react better to changes in the race. Controlling a rider like Tom Pidcock or Mathieu van der Poel, known for their expert handling of trajectories, becomes a completely new experience. Not only is it very different from previous years but also different to controlling less agile riders.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/0590111b0e944ee2a2d4577786a4186a7221d509.png[/img]

The previous Downhill rating influenced maximum downhill speed and had a very limited impact. Differentiating between riders only happened in high-speed sections. [i]Agility[/i], however, has an effect in all situations. The higher the rating (A+), the greater the rider's ability to turn quickly. This means the rider can take hairpin bends and tight corners at a higher speed than a rider with lower [i]Agility [/i](D). Therefore, every tight bend is a chance to put pressure on less agile riders and to weave in and out of the peloton to gain a better position for the final sprint, for example.

[previewyoutube=MfBYluSW98I;full][/previewyoutube]

Adding this new rating required adjustments to the behaviour of opponents so they can use this new ability better. A+ rated riders won't ride at their maximum rating throughout the race. After all, what's the point of a breakaway in a downhill when there are still 100km left until the finish line? The most agile riders will only use their maximum potential when it makes the most sense: during a downhill to the finish line, catching an opponent in the general classification, or during a mass sprint. However, a medium-rated rider (B, for example) can still try to put pressure on his breakaway teammates if he's the most agile among them.

The [i]Agility [/i]rating can be reduced by falls. In this situation, regardless of the rider's [i]Agility [/i]rating, it drops to the minimum tier for the rest of the stage. It then goes up a tier between each stage as the rider regains confidence in his abilities. To give an example, an A+ rider who has a fall will see his [i]Agility [/i]drop to D. His rating will then increase to C in the next stage, then B, and so on until he returns to A+ (provided he doesn't fall again in the meantime).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/1569187c61bb3c6f1e87d70e9b339f9a33acd5ef.png[/img]

[h2]MEDIUM MOUNTAIN NOTE[/h2]

As for the [i]Medium Mountain[/i] rating, it has been added to help calculate riders' energy consumption more accurately. The mathematical model is essentially based on the Flat, Hill, Mountain, Stamina and Resistance ratings, but these ratings didn't allow us to sufficiently rate all the riders' strengths. Between the Hill rating, which judges the ability to maintain effort for a short duration (around 2 min 30 sec) and the Mountain rating (for more sustained effort around 40 min long), we couldn't show that a rider performed well for more medium-length periods of effort (around 20 min) without setting one of the other two ratings too high.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43768775/68a94b3b467f1ce5c62e2831bdd9d485664dde57.png[/img]

Adding [i]Medium Mountain[/i] solves this issue and highlights certain riders' strengths. For example, for riders comfortable on medium mountains with category 1 or 2 climbs, but start to struggle on longer climbs, we can now lower the Mountain rating while keeping a higher [i]Medium Mountain[/i] rating to better target where these riders excel. In addition to this new rating, we've also reclassified certain stages into [i]Medium Mountains[/i] to make it clearer which stages are key ones for climbers and the general classification, and which are more open for baroudeurs.
